title: Royal commissions
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:38Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point is about Indigenous over-representation in custody and only mentions the Royal Commission as an example, so it does not teach what royal commissions are or how their powers work.

draft.title: Royal commissions
card: A royal commission is a public inquiry set up by government to investigate a matter of great public concern.
it can summon witnesses, require documents and hold public hearings. These powers are stronger than those of most other inquiries.
it reports its findings and recommends changes to law or practice. Government is not bound to adopt them all.
the Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse and the Royal Commission into Aged Care Quality and Safety led to reforms.
draft.remember: Royal commissions use strong powers to investigate and recommend, but government decides what to adopt.

a.q: What power makes a royal commission different from most other inquiries?
opts: It can summon witnesses and require documents
It can pass laws based on its findings
It can overturn court decisions it disagrees with
It can force government to adopt every recommendation
a.why: Royal commissions can compel witnesses and documents. They only recommend, so they cannot pass laws, which is the tempting wrong choice.
a.clue: Think about how it gathers evidence.

b.q: A royal commission into aged care publishes a report with many recommendations. What happens next?
opts: Government decides which recommendations to act on
The commission passes the changes in parliament
The courts review and enforce each recommendation
b.why: The commission recommends, and government and parliament choose what to adopt. Recommendations do not become law automatically, which is the tempting wrong choice.
b.clue: The commission reports but does not make law.

a.best: It can summon witnesses and require documents

b.best: Government decides which recommendations to act on

check.summary: No problems found. The card's facts on royal commission powers, the non-binding status of recommendations, and the two examples are accurate. Both questions have one clearly right answer, and the explanations match the card.
